rivalry.rationale: The India deodorant segment file is empty, but the evidence is not quite absent — it is cross-booked. Vini Cosmetics, whose Fogg brand is a deodorant business, sits in the repo under fragrances (FY25 operating revenue INR 1,200cr, MEDIUM, NET_REALISATION; KKR owns 54% at a US$1.2bn valuation), and india.json sizes India fragrances as 'perfume + DEODORANT combined' (US$2.6bn, LOW). That combined basket cannot be split, so there is no deodorant-only size and no deodorant-only share for any player. Rating rivalry off a basket that bundles two categories on a LOW-confidence figure would be a definitional error, so this force stays unrated even though a leading player is identifiable.

supplier_power.rationale: This is the one force the repo can support, and it rests on a finding that names the category directly: mass perfume and deodorant in India are domestically filled, in contrast to premium fragrance which is import-reliant on UAE, France and Germany. A domestically filled category sitting on top of India's documented third-party contract-manufacturing base — private-label houses taking orders from ~500 units, with specialty inputs from domestic makers such as Galaxy Surfactants and Fine Organics — means a deodorant brand owner has many interchangeable fillers and low switching cost. Suppliers hold little leverage. Rated THIN because the supporting evidence is a qualitative sourcing finding, not a deodorant-specific supply or cost DataPoint.

new_entrant_threat.rationale: Domestic fill plus a commoditised contract-manufacturing base points toward cheap entry, and the repo does record heavy capital moving into adjacent India D2C beauty (~US$757m over 18 months) — but none of that funding evidence is scoped to deodorants, and there is no deodorant market size against which to judge whether entry is attractive. The adjacent-category read is suggestive, not sufficient; it is recorded here rather than converted into a rating.

substitutes.rationale: The repo's one adjacent signal is that India's fragrance sizing bundles perfume with deodorant and body mist, which is a hint that the formats compete for the same demand — the fragrances Porter read treats that as directional substitution within the combined basket. Applied to deodorants alone it would be circular, since it is the same undivided basket, so this force is left unrated here.

overall.rationale: Not assessable as a standalone market. India deodorants is visible in this repo only through the fragrances basket it is bundled into and through one named player (Vini/Fogg) booked elsewhere; there is no deodorant-only size, growth, share or channel figure. The single defensible structural point is supply-side: the category is domestically filled and its manufacturing is commoditised, so an entrant would not be supplier-constrained. Everything that would determine whether entry is worthwhile — size, growth, who holds share, what the shelf costs — is missing, and the KR side is emptier still, so there is no corridor read either.
